analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/provider/cli-reference.md, in the "Runtime constants" table (base lines 1968-1969, head 1968-1971). The Coordinator reconnect backoff source now points to CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift. Two new rows are added: a backoff reset after a 60 s stable session, counted from the `register` frame, and a random 0-1 s reconnect wait after close code 1012 (service restart) without backoff growth. The WebSocket ping and pong row now cites CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift directly instead of "same". No code, configuration, endpoint, authorization or attestation behavior changes in the supplied evidence, and the surrounding base text is unchanged. The new rows describe provider reconnect behavior on TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket). Possible security effects, all unverified here because the Swift implementation is not supplied: (1) A coordinator-triggered 1012 close causes a fast, jittered reconnect with no backoff growth. This is a trusted coordinator, so it is not an adversary path, but reconnect storms are a possible availability concern. (2) The backoff reset is counted from the `register` frame. The next review should confirm that a fresh App Attest authorization, per-connection grant and endpoint-resumption (T-053) are still required on every reconnect, and that fast reconnects do not reuse stale authorization. This documentation edit does not show any regression, and it does not invalidate any threat-model assumption. Nothing indicates that a threat-model update is needed from this PR. The docs claims should be checked against CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift if that file is changed in a companion PR. No findings.
